title: Quintet members: Forrest, Persip, Elvin Jones, Flanagan, Hanna
summary: Edison recalls good Roulette records and the pianists and drummers who came through the band.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: (Recording interruption.)

I wanted to get that thought over, where I forgot it. We were talking about my band at that time, you know, and I was doing very well with that band, really was, with the quintet. Made some good records with Roulette.
Well, you and Jimmy went together well, as I remember.
Oh, yeah, a good twosome.
Jimmy was -- you know, he didn't get into that thing that he did with Basie later.
No, no, he got that little off the wall thing.
It was a show-off thing for a concert.
Yeah, yeah. But even a lot of the people who heard the concerts were saying, you know, that wasn't the Jimmy Forrest they had heard on records, or anything.
No, it was really a big ham, just like a drum solo. But it was a little embarrassing after you'd heard it once or twice. But, what the hell.
Well, I -- Charley Persip, that's the name of my drummer.
Oh, a good group.
Yeah, you know, when you get a certain age, your memory gets slow.
Well, so many names.
But Charlie Persip, he was in the band --
(Inaudible).
Yeah, and Elvin took his place.
Oh, Elvin took Persip's place, I see.
And Tommy Flanagan. Oh, I had a good band Oh, I really did. And then Roland Hanna, he came in after Tommy Flanagan and played with me. And --
How was he in those days?
Oh, he was playing fantastic. He was playing different all together. They played different in those days than they do now.
